items.problem: Migrated code used `new SolidColorBrush(Windows.UI.Colors.Green/Red)` and failed with CS0234 because the named-color class relocated to `Microsoft.UI.Colors` (requires `using Microsoft.UI;`). The mapping exists in the docs but the bootstrap script does not apply it, so it survives to a compile failure the agent must fix by hand.
items.evidence: session-log.txt:2622-2623 (CS0234 on Windows.UI.Colors), fixed at session-log.txt:2635-2641. Bootstrap rewrite log session-log.txt:279 shows only Windows.UI.Xaml was rewritten.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md:92 — the 'Namespace Mapping' table row `| Windows.UI.Colors | Microsoft.UI.Colors |`.
items.why_missed: under-emphasized — the entry is buried in a table introduced as 'All Windows.UI.Xaml.* namespaces move to Microsoft.UI.Xaml.*' (MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md:79). Windows.UI.Colors is NOT a `.Xaml.` namespace and Colors is a static class, not a namespace, so the framing hides it; and unlike Windows.UI.Xaml it is NOT auto-applied by Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 (line 126 only maps Windows.UI.Xaml), so nothing enforces it.
items.proposed_improvement: Promote this from doc-only to enforced tooling: extend Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1's mass-rewrite to also map the non-Xaml Windows.UI.* relocations `Windows.UI.Colors`->`Microsoft.UI.Colors` and `Windows.UI.ColorHelper`->`Microsoft.UI.ColorHelper` (word-boundary guarded so the unchanged `Windows.UI.Color` STRUCT is not touched), and add matching residueOnly patterns so Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 flags any leftover. Optionally note in the mapping table that Colors/ColorHelper are types (not namespaces) and Color the struct stays in Windows.UI.
items.generalizes: Status-block coloring via `SolidColorBrush(Colors.Green/Red)` is ubiquitous in the WinUI/UWP sample-template family (shared NotifyUser status block). Auto-applying the relocation removes a recurring hand-fixed CS0234 across essentially every sample that colors a status message.
